description: This round's FIND-019 fix correctly updated specs/verification-architecture.md's PROP-307c row (and its (8b) restatement) to carve step 9 out of the blanket 'steps 7-9 use the existing buildChildSpec-based REQ-305 failure path ... in every case no row anywhere claims status:"active"' claim -- but specs/behavioral-spec.md's own REQ-307 Acceptance Criteria (the Phase-1a source document PROP-307c is meant to formalize) was NOT touched by the fix commit (b0f120fa1, which only edited contracts/sprint-2.md and specs/verification-architecture.md) and still states, verbatim, the IDENTICAL disproven claim: '(b) for steps 7-9, the existing `buildChildSpec`-based failure path (REQ-305) is used; (c) in every case, no row anywhere claims `status:"active"` for that `child_id`.' This is directly falsified by the current, deliberately-implemented, and passing code: step 9 is two sub-operations (spawn-orchestrator.mjs:698 ledger 'active' append, then :700-736 citizen-registry append). The raw ledger-append failure sub-case (line 698) produces NO row at all and propagates uncaught -- confirmed passing test 'PROP-307c step 9 (REQ-305 ledger append itself fails) -> no row anywhere ever claims status:active' (spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs:287-304). The transient citizen-registry-append failure sub-case uses a THIRD mechanism, pending-registry-append.js's durable queue (never buildChildSpec), and its ledger row correctly DOES claim status:'active' -- confirmed passing test 'FIND-003: a transient citizens.json append failure (ENOTDIR) resolves status:"active" ...' (spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs:316-337). Neither sub-case matches behavioral-spec.md's own 'the existing buildChildSpec-based failure path (REQ-305) is used' description, and the transient sub-case directly contradicts its own '(c) in every case, no row anywhere claims status:active' clause. Since verification-architecture.md's PROP-307c explicitly cites itself as tracing to REQ-307's own Acceptance Criteria, leaving behavioral-spec.md un-corrected re-introduces the exact inaccuracy FIND-019 was meant to eliminate, one document upstream. A future reader of behavioral-spec.md alone (e.g. anyone re-deriving Phase 2a tests from REQ-307 without also cross-referencing the corrected verification-architecture.md) would still be misled into believing step 9 uses 'the existing buildChildSpec-based failure path' uniformly and can never leave an active row -- both false.

evidence.snippet: - An integration test triggers a failure at each of steps 1 through 9 in turn and confirms: (a) for steps 1-6 (**corrected, sprint-2 iteration 2, resolves FIND-S2-001**), a minimal `{child_id, status:"failed", attempted_ms, error}` row is appended directly (never via `buildChildSpec`); (b) for steps 7-9, the existing `buildChildSpec`-based failure path (REQ-305) is used; (c) in every case, no row anywhere claims `status:"active"` for that `child_id`.
evidence.testName: ~/anicca/skills/self/spawn/lib/__tests__/spawn-orchestrator.test.mjs:287-304 (raw ledger-append failure -> no row, rejects) and :316-337 (FIND-003 transient registry-append failure -> ledger row stays 'active', queued via pending-registry-append.js) -- both observed passing in this session's fresh `node --test` run (204/204)
